CSCU9M5 – Introduction to Machine Learning

Module Information

Module Title: Introduction to Machine Learning

Module Code: CSCU9M5

Teaching Institution: British University Vietnam (BUV)

Location/Method of Study: BUV, On Campus, Vietnam

Module Description

The study and use of machine learning has enjoyed a huge increase in popularity in recent years and can be found in systems as diverse as medical diagnosis systems and self-driving cars. Many modern artificial intelligence systems are driven by machine learning algorithms.

This module teaches the theory and practice of machine learning. You will learn the best practice for running a machine learning project and learn the theory behind the most common techniques, from regression to neural networks.

Systems that automatically make decisions (often about people) based on historical data need to be transparent and fair. This module will also consider the ethical aspects of modern machine learning and how to apply it without bias or inequality.

Additional Costs

There are no additional costs associated with this module.

Core Learning Outcomes

On successful completion of this module, students will be able to:

  1. Follow the correct methodology for building a machine learning solution.

  2. Evaluate machine learning algorithms to optimise their use for a given problem.

  3. Consider ethical and legal implications when implementing a machine learning solution.

Introductory Reading and Preparatory Work

There is no course textbook, but detailed lecture notes and learning materials will be provided through BUV Canvas.

The software used for this module is Orange, which can be downloaded here:

https://orangedatamining.com/

There are many excellent online resources for students who wish to explore machine learning further. You will be shown how to use these resources as the module progresses.

Recommended online resources include:

  • Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/

  • Machine Learning Mastery: https://machinelearningmastery.com/

Delivery

Learning Activity Hours Description
Scheduled Learning Hours 70 Large-group presentations or talks on particular topics.
Independent Study 130 Preparation for scheduled sessions, follow-up work, wider reading and practice, completion of assessment tasks, revision, accessing webinars and other materials available on demand.
Total Study Time 200

Assessment

The module is assessed through coursework and an examination.

Assessment Component Weighting Learning Outcomes Assessed
Coursework 50% 1–2
Examination (Canvas – off campus) 50% 2–3
Total 100%

Coursework: 50%

Examination: 50%

Further information about assessment requirements, submission deadlines and examination arrangements will be provided through BUV Canvas.
